title: TIC quarterly U.S. gross external debt (as-of 2027-09-30) — the next December edition, and the one whose published date proves the holiday rule
source: EST: home.treasury.gov/data/treasury-international-capital-tic-system/release-dates-of-tic-data, fetched direct 2026-09-09 (plain curl, HTTP 200, 111,181 bytes) by the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-12-31 initial-research adjacency sweep — its 2027 table's December row reads '16 | 16 | 30', the 30 placed in the fourth column ('Quarterly: U.S. gross external debt at end of previous quarter') by parsing cells by index. THE 30 IS THE POINT: the page's own rule is the last business day of the quarter, and 2027-12-31 is a Friday. It is not the last business day because 2028-01-01 falls on a Saturday, which under 5 U.S.C. 6103 makes Friday 2027-12-31 the OBSERVED New Year's Day holiday — so the last business day of December 2027 is Thursday 2027-12-30, exactly what Treasury published. Reproduced mechanically this session from the statute's rules rather than a holiday list. Filed estimate per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep; the date is Treasury's own and is not in doubt. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: DISCOVERED during the tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-12-31 initial research (2026-09-09) and proposed on two specific grounds, where the sibling tic-quarterly-external-debt-2027-03-31 explicitly DECLINED to propose the 2027 editions because they were checkpoints of nothing it registered. Both grounds are checkpoints of tests this proposer registers. FIRST: it is the next out-of-sample observation of FT-tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-12-31-2, the December-fragility test. December is the only edition of the four that has ever been materially late (12 of 15 at offset +0, and the series' only two slips beyond two days are its +31 in 2019 and +16 in 2026, both following a long funding lapse in the reference-to-release window), and n is 15 — one more observation moves it. SECOND: its published date is the empirical proof of an arithmetic point this proposer's leg 1 uses to CORRECT a sibling census. tic-quarterly-external-debt-2026-09-30 read December as carrying two '-1' early publications (2021-12-30 and 2024-12-30); recomputing the holiday rule from statute leaves only one (2024-12-30), because 2022-01-01 was a Saturday and therefore 2021-12-31 was an observed federal holiday, making 2021-12-30 the last business day and the publication +0 rather than -1. Treasury's own 2027 schedule prints 30 for exactly that reason, which is as close to a primary-sourced confirmation of the arithmetic as this series offers. Impact LOW and symbols empty on the standing grounds: no accompanying press release, data a quarter stale at print, no house playbook keyed to a macro release. Note it inherits this edition's two peculiarities — a 10 AM ET publication inside the cash session rather than 4 PM, and a reference-to-release window that always contains the October 1 fiscal-year boundary. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
